Using device: cuda

Full dataset: X=torch.Size(\[10000, 32]), y=torch.Size(\[10000])





**INTERPRETATION OF w\_t AND DISTANCES**



**w\_t = parameter vector after t gradient steps.**

**w\*  = final iterate after 500 steps (used as an approximation of the limit).**



We measure optimization in the Hilbert projective metric:



**- d\_H(w\_t, w\*): contraction toward the limit direction.**

**- d\_H(w\_t, w\_0): loss of dependence on the initial direction.**

**- d\_H(w\_{t+1}, w\_t): projective "speed" of each update.**



These three sequences allow us to distinguish different types of cone

dynamics (PF-type contraction vs. geodesic-like motion).



The following notation might be helpful:



**- n = sample size**

**- l2\_reg = coefficient of regularization parameter**

**- D\_H is the Hilbert projective metric**



**d\_H(w\_t, w\*) is like a arithmetic sequence in this experiment(after first serveral terms, namely erotic)**
